workflow_runs.name: CI
workflow_runs.display_title: Add Option-B trusted financial system, migration hardening, and release verification

head_commit.message:
fix: use the user's local "today" in the trusted function, not UTC

executeFinancialOperation decided which date is the user's current day
(the only date that may still be priced from the live tracker config) in
UTC. Away from UTC, for several hours around the day boundary it treated
the user's current day as a past one, leaving its spend/savings
unresolved.

- Clients send currentTrackingDate (device wall clock + dayStartHour, the
  rule every write already uses): web via one trustedExecute helper for
  all 8 call sites, Kotlin via the view model's gateway wrapper.
- The server accepts it only if it is the current tracking date somewhere
  on Earth right now (UTC-12..UTC+14) and rejects anything else
  (IMPLAUSIBLE_CURRENT_TRACKING_DATE). It is excluded from the operation
  fingerprint, so a retry across midnight is the same operation. Clients
  that omit it keep the old UTC behaviour.
- A stored profile timezone was rejected: any valid zone could be chosen,
  so it would allow the same window while adding schema.

Tests: validation unit tests (zones either side of midnight UTC, midnight
day start, rejection, fallback), emulator integration (accepted /
rejected / retry applies once), web routing tests with a local-time
clock, Kotlin view-model assertion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: trusted account deletion for MIGRATING/OPTION_B accounts

A locked account could not delete itself: the rules deny its financial
deletes and (since the delete-and-recreate fix) its profile delete, so the
client-side wipe failed partway.

- functions: new deleteAccountData callable recursively deletes the
  CALLER's users/{uid} tree (uid from verified auth only; no target
  parameter). Requires a sign-in within 5 minutes (requireRecentLogin),
  matching the clients' reauth-before-delete step, so a leaked ID token
  alone cannot wipe an account. The Auth user is still deleted by the
  client afterwards.
- web + Kotlin: deleteAllUserData routes MIGRATING/OPTION_B accounts to
  the callable and attempts no direct delete; LEGACY keeps the
  client-side wipe (works on Spark without Cloud Functions).
- Kotlin: FirebaseTrustedFinancial now defaults to europe-west1 (it
  defaulted to the SDK's us-central1, where no callables exist).
- Tests: emulator integration (locked account with data in every
  subcollection is fully deleted; unauthenticated call rejected; another
  user untouched), recent-login unit test, web routing tests, and device
  testN (locked account routes to the trusted delete).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
ci(android): run the trusted-callable instrumentation tests in CI

testL/testM call executeFinancialOperation on-device but had never
completed a CI run (every run since they were added was cancelled by a
newer push). The first full run failed both:

- The Functions SDK rejects the placeholder API key in CI's
  google-services.json ("Please set a valid API key"). Use a
  syntactically valid, clearly fake key for the demo project.
- CI started only the Firestore/Auth emulators. Install functions/
  dependencies, start the Functions emulator (port 5001, nodejs22), wait
  for "All emulators ready", and adb-reverse tcp:5001.
- ownerPatch seeded the hardcoded project tabakpp-ff036, a namespace the
  CI app (demo-tabakpp-test) never reads; seed the app's own project id,
  and fail loudly on a non-2xx response.
- testL/testM used 2099 dates, which the trusted function now rejects
  (FUTURE_DATE); use past dates.

Verified locally with CI's exact google-services.json and emulator
project: 28/28 instrumentation tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
